lower-klamath-national-wildlife-refuge.note: T.R. bird reservation. Both passes agree.

hawaiian-islands-national-wildlife-refug.note: T.R. bird reservation. Both passes agree.

events.name: Sanibel National Wildlife Refuge
events.text: At the urging of Jay Norwood "Ding" Darling, the Sanibel National Wildlife Refuge was established through a lease agreement with the State of Florida under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act.

authority.citation: Lease agreement with the State of Florida under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act

sources.name: FWS ServCat: J.N. "Ding" Darling NWR Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2010)
Island Reporter / captivasanibel.com, letter, June 2010: When did the islands officially become special?

events.note: FWS gives December 1, 1945. The only non-FWS source read is a 2010 reader letter that says 1945; too weak to confirm. A popular site claims President Truman bought the land; no evidence of that was found, and it should not be repeated. Later renamed for Darling; renaming date not verified.

j-n-ding-darling-national-wildlife-refug.note: Year 1945 is consistent; a stronger non-FWS source is needed.

events.name: Columbia White Tailed Deer Sanctuary
events.text: The Fish and Wildlife Service bought an 845-acre first parcel in December 1971, establishing a sanctuary for the endangered Columbian white-tailed deer along the lower Columbia River.

authority.citation: Administrative establishment by land purchase (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service)

sources.name: FWS ServCat: Lewis and Clark NWR and Julia Butler Hansen Refuge CCP/EIS (2010)

events.note: FWS CCP: first parcel bought December 1971 as the 'Columbia White Tailed Deer Sanctuary'; renamed Columbian White-tailed Deer National Wildlife Refuge by July 1972. The later renaming for Representative Julia Butler Hansen was not verified.

julia-butler-hansen-refuge-for-the-colum.note: No independent non-FWS source was found in this pass; needs one (for example the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission's annual report, a Federal Register notice signed outside FWS, or a contemporary newspaper) before publication.

events.name: North Platte Reservation
events.text: President Woodrow Wilson reserved four Reclamation Service reservoirs west of Scottsbluff, Nebraska, including Lakes Alice and Minatare and Winters Creek Lake, as the North Platte Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, by Executive Order 2446.

sources.name: FWS ServCat: Establishment Documents - North Platte Reservation (printed order, 21 August 1916, No. 2446)
FWS ServCat: North Platte NWR Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2001)
American Presidency Project: Proclamation 2416 (July 25, 1940), renaming North Platte Reservation

events.note: The FWS file holds a printed copy of the order (No. 2446, 21 August 1916, signed Woodrow Wilson). Proclamation 2416 confirms the name 'North Platte Reservation' but not the date. No non-FWS copy of EO 2446 was found (not on the Presidency Project or Wikisource).

north-platte-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Strong primary evidence, but only FWS-hosted; needs a non-FWS copy of EO 2446 to confirm.
